en.title: ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace: What Counts?
en.titleCore: ChatGPT Enterprise on AWS Marketplace and what counts toward your AWS commitment
en.description: Which ChatGPT Enterprise charges count toward AWS EDP or PPA? See how eligibility, shared caps, invoice timing and payable shortfalls affect the real cost.
en.body:
ChatGPT Enterprise is available through AWS Marketplace, and eligible charges can count toward an AWS Enterprise Discount Program or private pricing commitment. What counts depends on the accepted offer, covered payer, recognition rules and remaining Marketplace cap. An invoice can be payable in full while only part of it reduces the AWS commitment.

What did OpenAI launch on AWS Marketplace?

On November 9, 2026, OpenAI announced that organizations can buy ChatGPT Enterprise through their AWS purchasing and billing relationship. The listing names OpenAI as the seller, identifies the product as SaaS deployed on AWS, and says spend can count toward an AWS EDP or PPA commitment. The suite includes Chat, Work, Codex and dots. OpenAI says the feature release schedule is the same as for direct Enterprise customers. Eligible customers can also access ChatGPT for Healthcare and Financial Services through Marketplace. Confirm those products on their own offer documents. OpenAI’s announcement · ChatGPT Enterprise Marketplace listing.

The listing uses a private-offer quote. It publishes no per-seat price, minimum seat count, included usage schedule, or universal discount. AWS Marketplace private offers carry negotiated pricing and terms and are sent to a designated AWS account. Compare quotes on the same seats, term, payment dates, usage entitlements, true-ups, support and renewal terms. Listing and pricing · AWS private-offer guide.

What actually counts toward an AWS EDP or PPA?

Start with the eligible Marketplace charges under the accepted offer, in a covered account, that AWS recognizes in the applicable commitment period. Then apply any credit rate, shared cap, or other treatment in your signed AWS agreement. OpenAI’s announcement describes eligible spend. The listing says eligible consumption counts subject to your agreement. AWS also evaluates eligibility per product when several products are purchased together. Neither public source publishes a buyer-specific allocation. OpenAI’s eligibility wording · AWS on eligible Marketplace drawdown · AWS on eligibility in bundled offers.

Charge or routeHow to treat it
ChatGPT Enterprise on the linked AWS Marketplace offerEligible product route. Confirm covered line items, payer, amount and recognition period with AWS.
ChatGPT Enterprise purchased directly from OpenAIAn OpenAI invoice is outside this Marketplace route. Any direct arrangement needs its own written terms.
OpenAI API usage or credits purchased separatelySeparate product and billing path. The Enterprise offer does not establish eligibility for them.
OpenAI models through Amazon BedrockSeparate AWS service charges. Apply the AWS agreement rules for those charges independently of ChatGPT seats.
Seat true-ups, extra usage, add-ons or servicesInclude only the items the private offer and AWS terms confirm. Request itemized treatment for onboarding, support and reseller charges.
Tax, credits, refunds and currency conversionReconcile separately. Confirm the qualifying basis, conversion convention and adjustment timing in writing.

EDP and PPA here refer to the organization’s negotiated AWS spending commitment. A Savings Plan applies to eligible AWS usage under its own terms. AWS promotional credits are a separate payment mechanism, and AWS’s standard terms exclude Marketplace charges unless AWS authorizes otherwise. Count the Enterprise invoice as a cash payable and record any commitment drawdown separately. AWS Savings Plans · AWS promotional credit terms.

Does 25% apply to the invoice or to the commitment?

A Marketplace cap limits the total contribution from Marketplace purchases against the defined AWS commitment base. A recognition rate determines how much of an eligible transaction can contribute before the cap. These are different numbers. Cisco’s historical AWS sales material illustrates full recognition of eligible spend paired with a 25% cap on contribution to the commitment. Treat that as evidence of how the two percentages can coexist, and use the signed agreement to determine whether your offer has that structure, a different cap, or a carve-out. Cisco’s 2023 AWS partner material · AWS on customer-specific commitment terms.

For a straightforward agreement with one shared cap, model the new contribution as min(eligible charges × recognition rate, max(0, cap − other recognized Marketplace spend)). Use the eligible charge base after the adjustments your agreement specifies. Include already planned Marketplace renewals in the forecast if they compete for that same cap. The table shows how different contract terms or transaction details can change the result. Every amount and rate is illustrative.

Scenario on the $120k eligible baseRate assumedCap roomRecognized
No binding Marketplace cap100%At least $120k$120k
Shared cap almost full100%$40k$40k
Lower recognition rate50%At least $120k$60k
Cap exhausted or payer out of scope100% if otherwise eligible$0 or ineligible$0

Suppose the annual commitment is $1 million, with a $250,000 Marketplace cap, $730,000 of qualifying native AWS spend and $210,000 already recognized from other Marketplace purchases. That leaves $40,000 under the Marketplace cap and a $60,000 projected shortfall. If a $120,000 ChatGPT invoice is eligible at a 100% recognition rate, only $40,000 can contribute. You still pay $120,000 for ChatGPT, and the projected AWS shortfall falls to $20,000.

When does the spend count?

Separate the offer acceptance date, subscription start, invoice date, payment date and the AWS commitment recognition period. AWS documents both upfront invoicing and seller-defined installment dates for contract-based private offers. The payment schedule shows when AWS bills the purchase. Ask AWS which event its commitment statement uses, what time zone applies near a period boundary, and how refunds or amendments are reflected. A multiyear total contract value on the offer is insufficient to forecast recognized spend in the current year. AWS Marketplace billing schedules and currencies · Future-dated agreements.

For example, take a $120,000 contract and assume AWS counts charges in the period they are invoiced, unused cap room does not carry forward, and you have $40,000 of room in period one and $90,000 in period two. Billing the whole deal in period one yields $40,000 of contribution. Two $60,000 invoices in different periods yield $100,000 in total. The second schedule does not fix a period-one shortfall beyond the same $40,000. Model the cash value of each period’s contribution separately.

When does Marketplace reduce the total bill?

Recognized spend has cash value to the extent it avoids a payable shortfall. Suppose the direct quote is $105,000 and Marketplace is $120,000 for the same terms. In the example above, Marketplace avoids $40,000 of a shortfall that would otherwise be payable dollar for dollar. Its $15,000 quote premium buys $40,000 in avoided charges, making incremental cash outlay $25,000 lower. If your forecast already clears the AWS commitment, Marketplace costs $15,000 more on those quotes before other differences.

Illustrative caseDirect quote + AWS shortfallMarketplace quote + AWS shortfallCash difference
$60k payable shortfall before purchase$105k + $60k = $165k$120k + $20k = $140kMarketplace is $25k lower
No projected shortfall$105k + $0 = $105k$120k + $0 = $120kDirect is $15k lower

Where the shortfall is payable dollar for dollar, the avoided amount is the lesser of the recognized contribution and the payable shortfall. Compare it with the Marketplace price premium plus any incremental tax, fees, currency or financing cost. If the AWS deal has carry-forward, true-up or different shortfall settlement terms, model the actual cash consequence instead. Check whether another software renewal could close the same gap at lower incremental cost. A dollar of cap can only be used once.

One common reporting error is to subtract $40,000 from the SaaS invoice and also subtract $40,000 from the AWS shortfall. The invoice is still $120,000. Apply the $40,000 once, against the shortfall. Track recognized commitment dollars, actual avoided shortfall and software invoice spend as separate metrics.

What should procurement ask AWS and OpenAI before accepting?

  1. Get the offer in writing. Confirm the Marketplace product, offer ID, buyer account, seller of record, invoice currency, service term, seats, included usage, overages, support, credits and payment schedule. Ask how a direct Enterprise agreement would transition, including the old renewal date and any overlapping obligations.
  2. Ask AWS for a period-by-period allocation. Provide the offer ID, buyer and payer account IDs, legal entity and line items. Ask for the eligible charge basis, rate, cap base and remaining headroom, estimated recognized amount per invoice, recognition event and period, and tax, FX, credit and refund treatment. Confirm where the recognized amount will appear after billing.
  3. Compare equivalent economics. Run the direct and Marketplace quotes against base, low and high forecasts for native AWS spend and other Marketplace renewals. Compare payment schedules on the same dates and scope. Assign an internal software owner, cost center and purchase order.
  4. Check governance separately. The listing names OpenAI as processor and AWS as one of its subprocessors. Marketplace procurement does not guarantee all data stays on AWS infrastructure or inside your AWS account. Confirm at-rest residency and inference residency for the enabled features and regions. Marketplace data handling disclosure · OpenAI residency documentation.

A concrete request for your AWS account team is “For this offer and payer, how much from each scheduled invoice will count against each commitment period, and where can we verify that posting?” Ask the team to call out any line item that receives different treatment. Have the relevant commercial owner confirm the result against the signed agreement before budgeting savings.

How can FinOps verify the credit after purchase?

  1. Save the accepted offer and agreement with the payer and subscribing account, legal entity, seller, dates and invoice schedule. AWS Organizations can accept private offers from a management or member account. Confirm the specific payer and member accounts covered by your commercial terms. AWS buyer account guidance.
  2. Use Marketplace Procurement insights to find the agreement and actual product spend. Match invoices by payer, invoicing entity, invoice ID and billing period in AWS Data Exports CUR 2.0. The billing entity helps separate Marketplace transactions from other AWS charges. AWS says the invoice ID remains blank until the report is final. Procurement insights · CUR 2.0 billing fields.
  3. Reconcile the billed amount to the amount AWS shows or confirms for the commitment period. Keep separate columns for gross charge, adjustments, qualifying base, recognized amount, cap remaining and projected payable shortfall. Invoice data proves billing. The commitment statement or written AWS reconciliation proves drawdown.

Sources were checked on November 9, 2026. Public evidence establishes the purchase route and product-level eligibility. The examples use synthetic quotes and commitment terms. The private offer and signed AWS agreement supply the amounts for a real decision.

faq.question: Does AWS Marketplace ChatGPT Enterprise spend count toward AWS EDP?
faq.answer: The product listing says it can count toward EDP or PPA. The eligible line items, payer, recognition period and remaining Marketplace allowance determine the amount AWS applies.

faq.question: Does the Marketplace cap mean only 25% of the ChatGPT invoice counts?
faq.answer: A cap expressed as a share of the commitment limits aggregate Marketplace contribution. A separate recognition rate determines how much of each eligible dollar can contribute. Use your signed terms for both.

faq.question: Can AWS promotional credits pay the ChatGPT Enterprise Marketplace invoice?
faq.answer: AWS promotional credit terms generally exclude Marketplace charges unless AWS authorizes them. Commitment drawdown is a separate calculation from paying an invoice with promotional credits.

faq.question: Is there a public ChatGPT Enterprise price in AWS Marketplace?
faq.answer: The listing requests a private offer and provides custom pricing based on requirements and eligibility. Use the issued quote to compare prices, payment schedules and terms.

faq.question: Does signing a multiyear private offer count the full value immediately?
faq.answer: Confirm the recognition event and commitment period with AWS. Private offers can have upfront or installment billing, and the total signed value alone cannot establish what AWS will recognize in the current period.
